item.title: Re: Festive Jello Strikes Back
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'm largely in agreement with Grigori here; what you've got is a pretty bland monster that might have been alright on the mainsite a decade ago, but the concept as it is won't do well on the mainsite today given we have thousands of similarly dangerous entities written, many of them with more narrative to them than just "it wreaks havoc and presumably a GoI made it".

I'm also unsure about the cognitohazard/pheromone explanation, since if the jello itself is constantly secreting the pheromones, how does that trigger its own response only when "prey" is nearby? The backstory of the investigation also makes the Foundation look rather incompetent—if one field agent already went missing, why didn't the later ones take better precautions when investigating? Having a live body cam feed, radioing in their status every few minutes or so, even just sending a drone into the location to scout. It seems kind of silly that the agents' disappearance would be entirely unexplained and necessitate an MTF be sent in to do the same job.

The description of the anomaly being jello containing human remains just makes me think of the Gelatinous Cube from Dungeons & Dragons: https://roll20.net/compendium/dnd5e/Gelatinous%20Cube it also seems a little odd that it would specifically need to be festive jello; I personally don't know anyone who actually eats jello specifically for the holidays. I feel like if you really want to make this specific monster workable, you'd need to make it more distinct from the popular D&D monsters and also have an in-universe reason for why it exists the way it does. Otherwise you have something that's relatively forgettable and will be more likely compared to more interesting monsters in popular culture, rather than being interesting on its own merit.

The audience is constantly kept engaged by a linear narrative starting off with mystery that later unfolds into a deeper investigation of the SCP's origins.

This is a big, big assumption to make here, especially since you haven't finalized what the motives of the GoI are, and it's still unclear what the point of the anomaly actually is. I myself don't really think a draft of the material currently presented would be engaging, since the core anomaly is fairly boring, the effects seem rather randomly applied and not thematically related, and the backstory is rather vague. You'd need to address all of these issues before I would think it reasonable to expect the audience to be "constantly engaged".

item.title: Re: Mommy, Daddy, look! A rainbow!
item.content:encoded:
Hello jacked-anime-cole! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: Eight human-looking entities created when shining a specific spotlight at a special prism.

While the premise sounds doable, there isn't enough specific information here to really get an idea of what the skip is. The concept doesn't really show what the skips motives or purpose is, or expand upon the base idea. Overall there isn't much to get invested in here as the concept is too vague.

-Some general things to expand on:

-What are these entities
-why are they important
-what is their purpose
-what part does the prism play in all of this
-why should I as the reader care about the concept? what will make me invested?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: There is none yet, but will be very soon! :)

I would highly recommend developing some sort of narrative before posting, as they help give a direction to the concept and can help with audience engagement. Articles featuring a narrative tend to favoured by modern audiences, which has more or less lead to Articles with a narrative becoming the standard. -the narrative doesn't need to be super detailed and long, short stories also work very well (it mostly comes down to execution).

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A corrosive light from a spotlight and a hazardous prism come together to shine eight colours on a wall, from Red all the way to Pink.

This feels closer to a brief summary of the skip, as there isn't much other than the skips characteristics and functions shown here. What about this will make me invested? what are the implications of this? how should this make the reader feel?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

Notes:

Additional Notes: I need help with the attention grabber and the central narrative. If anyone has ideas PLEASE tell me them! Thank you!

Generally speaking, I would recommend expanding upon what you currently have. Try to get an idea on what the skips end goal is (or purpose is), and use that to get an idea on the overall narrative and central conflict.- don't be afraid to experiment with different endings or motives!

- Try to get an idea on where the narrative will start and end, that way the middle act and conflict will be easier to put together.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.content:encoded:
It's a chemically changing rock. Name is work in progress, and I'm not too happy with the discovery, so any help/suggestions would be nice

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/intriguing?

Page Layout (Optional): Standard article. After description, will go over discovery, and after discovery will then go over test logs.

Elevator Pitch: It's a tall rock that slightly twists. The tip of it will be called element A, and the base of it will be called element B. If an object touches the tip, element A changes into the majority of the atoms in that object. There are various things that cause a teleport event, but when that happens, the spire disappears and reappears at a random spot on the earth. element B then becomes the old element A, element A becomes the closest solid element near the tip, and the spire absorbs every current element B atom in a 1km radius.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: It was discovered when a redacted reality bender started rampaging, and along with various other items it created the spire. Some clean up MTF member accidentally touches the tip with his glove, and his glove disappears along with the spire. It's found in some town where around half of the people there dropped dead and withered on the spot, because the glove was mostly carbon, and all the carbon was stolen from their bodies. The spire is found in the town, and it's got a carbon base with a solid oxygen tip (from the oxygen in the granite that built the town)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The rules for the spire are pretty strict, so it's like a constant reminder that whatever the old tip was, all those atoms could immediately disappear in the center of a city, but it could also appear in the center of a forest, and be difficult to track down, so I feel that would draw people into the story. Also there's a mention near the beginning about testing being discontinued, so I feel people would want to see why

Additional Notes: The things that cause a teleportation event(work in progress name) are: The tip is touched with the same majority atom as the tip already had, so instead of staying the same it teleports. 108 hours pass without a tip change. If the tip is a radioactive element, the moment an atom in it decays, it undergoes the event (which is pretty much instantly). If the tip and base are the same element, it undergoes the event. If the tip is helium, it undergoes the event. I can explain more, as a lot of the info had to be cut down due to size limit.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

While we offer some leeway for stuff that is just linked and is hosted offsite, you must make it clear that that content is not under the site's license. An example that comes to mind is 248-J.

In this scenario, however, because of the volume of videos you'll be using in your piece and how they appear to be significantly important to your piece, I will ask as a member of the Licensing Team that you do not do such a thing unless you explicitly release those videos under a CC BY-SA 3.0 compliant license. As it's unknown how important those 37 videos of yours will be to the narrative of your article, I am forced to prohibit linking them unless you are either willing to release the videos under a Creative Commons license, or can state that their inclusion is not central to the article itself.

item.title: Re: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA
item.content:encoded:
I actually like this one. You've taken an old critter and had some fun with it. It would be interesting to see the ads be a sort of cognitohazard, in that once someone sees an ad they are compelled to answer the ad and follow through on it.

This would force The Foundation to make a D-Class follow the ad, and then an MTF follow the D-Class to the sirens. Of course, this could create an interesting chase as the sirens see the MTF coming from a mile away. The Foundation would then administer some sort of anti-memetic to relieve the stress in the D-Class, who is unable to complete his quest.

Of course, the MTF could lose the D-Class, and when they followed the tracker find the corpse of the D-Class, forcing them to repeat the process until they find the sirens.

While I'm not sure you really need paratech here (the sirens' intent should be enough), another option would be to have the sirens run a newspaper and run the ads themselves. That not only gives them greater control over the ads, but also gives them a better lead time if someone starts investigating the ads.

You've got a great idea; I hope it works out!

item.title: Re: Concept : Ever Burning Flames.
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Okay, let's see what we have…

The core idea is that the flames are made out of something else and a meteor had landed into a building in a city in China. The flames were green. The flames could burn down anything after they had tested it. It then spreads to a entire city. Then, the foundation notices it hasn't been stopped. The meteor that landed, had a gauntlet of the green flame after being collected by the foundation. There was a drawing of meteor dropping and a city burning. The zone that was burning was contained.

So, just for me to restate; This is a green fire that never can be extinguished or stop growing. The ideas alone is kinda boring. Is there anything else to it?

A journal about a person that was trapped in the zone that was being flamed. He and his family escaped there apartment as the fire was spreading. Then, it shows there experience about being in a zone of infinite place. The person who was writing it, eventually dies from starvation. The notebook was found near the border. The fire already has spread to the entire city so most of the information was burned.

A journal of survivors certainly can give a good narrative. But why should I be excited for a survivor in a burning fire? Also, what's the "infinite place". How did the notebook get to the border and why would the Foundation be interested in one burning book from presumably thousands of burning items?

Overall Thoughts: The idea is rather boring and I don't quiet understand how the Foundation would obtain the journal. I would suggest having a source to the anomaly and have a series of logs with a MTF attempting to contain the anomaly.

- Close

item.title: Re: Sentient, climate-conscious tree
item.content:encoded:
You're sort of approaching this one from the wrong angle: It sounds like the tree is using the kids to promote eco-friendly beliefs. The kids see the tree and it implants a compulsion that the kids then act on, with the moss being the way it communicates.

This places it in the category of cognitohazard, where the tree is using a sense (the sight of the moss) to manipulate the kids. Even if that manipulation has a good intention, The Foundation tends to take a dim view of SCPs that psychically manipulate people. As such, your hook should be "Well-intentioned tree becomes a force in local politics to better the environment, forcing a moral conflict between its good intentions and the way it's doing it."

That creates a much stronger narrative and shifts the tree from being "just interesting" and "very interesting". It also forces The Foundation to make some interesting choices, especially considering how hard it is to move the tree. Do they attempt to chop it down in order to neutralize it, fence it off and allow it to live, or something else?

There's also the question if the moss retains it ability to affect the kids if it is removed from the tree, and if the tree can see through the moss. If it does, then it could be the start of a new druidic cult of sorts.

Regardless, you have a good start. Now have some fun with it!

item.title: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA
item.content:encoded:
A coven of sirens- yes, like the mythological Greek kind- find themselves adapting to the modern climate in order to seek their prey.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Comedy, mainly, but not in an un-serious manner.

Elevator Pitch: You know those clearly fake ads you get on nsfw websites? The ones that’re like “HOT SINGLES IN YOUR AREA”, et cetera. Yeah. Those, but anomalous, and set up by Sirens, as in the type that’d lure sailors to death. The ad, if loaded on a page, would display a message along the lines of “10 HOT (xyz) WITHIN (distance)! TEXT NOW!”

+ show block
– hide block

As time went by, the distance would gradually decrease, and the number increase. This would culminate in the subject being ambushed, and then… well, consumed, by a number of horrible, vaguely humanoid fishy-people.

The Foundation would later track these ads to a certain location, and, unable to block the ads via webcrawlers or other non-anomalous means, would send in an MTF team to find out what’s going on. There’s an exploration log, and the anomaly is accidentally neutralised when the coven of sirens panics upon realising there’s angry fellows with guns in the hideout and collapses the building in order to escape, breaking all of their paratech that let them make and maintain the anomalous ads in the first place.

Central Narrative: The context behind this strange new manner of Greek monsters luring in prey is simply that people don’t usually fall for the ole’ “Sing to the sailors until they follow you and drown” trick, and they’ve had to resort to new and unusual means of tracking targets. Inkeeping with the tradition of luring sailors in with beautiful songs and false faces, they decide to essentially hijack NSFW spam ads, which ends up working pretty well.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As far as I’m aware, nobody’s done sirens as an SCP before, and beyond that, the concept of the fake ads on the sides of sketchy sites actually being dangerous beyond just giving your computer malware is a little spine-chilling. And also really funny, when you think about it.

Additional Notes: As this would be my first SCP, essentially any critique at all would be greatly appreciated.

item.content:encoded:
Why the tree would want children to protect it even after it has adquired information about whats happening to the world? The best course of action would be try to influenciate important people, like company managers or political partys.

I don't know, I think you're trying to explain a behavir, that should even be about our survival, using an SCP. Like its not normal. Thats an approach you should be careful with.

But I really like the eggoistic self survival persona you gave to the tree, since it made a contract with the foundation to be protected and not in behalf of any other plant.

I would suggest giving it a more horror like style. It could be inside a forest, and all the other trees could have been people. If you still want to maintain that enviromental idea, it would even make more sence if transforms people into other trees since its reducing the number of humans that it ostracize and also reflorestating.

The trees could even bleed if they are cut.

Have a great day!

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find a list of ways to contact reviewers in this thread: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

item.title: Sentient, climate-conscious tree
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Dunno

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A tree that is intelligent and sentient and has an effect on kids and teens that come into direct contact with it that causes them to be protective of it and environmentally conscious. A small number of these young people are able to communicate with it by writing on its branches or trunk and receiving a reply written in moss that only they can interpret. It caused a month long strike by these affected youths that the foundation struggled to break up.

Central Narrative: The tree became anomalous in the late 1800s when the industrial revolution was pumping out pollution. It became more active in the past few decades after it was told by affected kids about climate change and deforestation and so on. The tree is pretty angry and upset at all this so when someone decides to cut it down to build on the land, the tree goes into full rage mode and for four straight weeks all affected kids surrounded the tree and refused to move, not even to eat or sleep though they had no symptoms of death from this. The tree eventually chills out after the foundation uses one of kids as a messenger to talk with it and promise (on behalf of the foundation) to look after it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Poor tree doesn’t want to die. Makes sure everyone knows it.

Additional Notes: Criticise away!

item.title: Re: Book of the undead
item.content:encoded:
Ok, it's something!
But again I must ask, why? What kind of story are you trying to tell?
A simple ancient artifact? You can definitely do more with this, I feel. Here's a bunch of other questions to help you expand the idea:

What was this object originally used for?
Why does it revive everyone into hostile mutants?
What is this creature? How does it protect the object? Why?
How was this object hidden from everyone? Furthermore, did nobody find it, ever? If they did, what happened?

Again, just a few questions to help you flesh stuff out, but don't stop at those! My suggestion for ideas is to keep building them. Don't force ideas, but if ideas come, see if they can be worked in.

item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5179 is a interdimensional anomaly located in ██████. The project can only be seen on the night of the new moon. Due to it's anomalous properties, anyone enter SCP-5179 will turn into SCP-5179-1 and the process is irreversible.

Deleted at -17 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

EthanolC2H5OH

+ show block
– hide block

It's a cool idea albeit executed poorly, there is a lot of typos and grammar errors that need to be addressed and the weird white boxes make the page cluttered and difficult to read as you're constantly switching between the two parts of the article. The whole 'Youth passes as a fleeting river, star lies in the silver flower.' is quite a good addition and the fact it addresses the reader is a brilliant touch. Overall, a good concept executed and worded poorly.

JakdragonX

+ show block
– hide block

I wanted to love this, so, so badly. In truth, I really like this concept, and the disjointed aspect of the white boxes sort of peering into… "someone's (???)" inner life in this town of Astra was fun, albeit a bit off-toned.

However, unfortunately, there's just a massive level of "clutter" that can't be ignored (not even when it comes to the formatting.) The ending is also a bit… flat? Like, I can sort of see what you're attempting with it, but frankly the characters are somewhat baseless that its hard to keep track. It kind of reads like a "trying-to-remember" dream sequence, which may be intentional, but for myself personally it's hard to associate.

I really want to love this, and I see some potential. I'd love to see this rewritten and reworked, since it's just conceptually pleasing for me personally.

EDIT: Should also mention that I like the fourth-wall break (I'm always a sucker for them), but after re-reading, this time it feels entirely off-base from everything else, not to mention gimmicky at best.

SCP-5461-1 is a small plastic bag, of the variety usually used in candy stores to put self-served candy inside. Written on the "front" of the bag in Sharpietm brand marker is the incription, 'yumy gummie bear by dado'. SCP-5461-1 holds a small amount of gummy bears, which are classified SCP-5461-2. SCP-5461-2 are mildly sapient, and possess different amounts of sentience,depending on their color. they are also capable of giving artificial feelings to those who consume.
